morphogenGradientLab.title: The French-flag rule
morphogenGradientLab.subtitle: A gradient tells cells what to become
morphogenGradientLab.hint: Drag the decay length and the two thresholds. The same row of cells re-sorts into three fates — no cell is told individually what to be; each just reads the concentration where it sits.
morphogenGradientLab.aria: A morphogen concentration curve above a row of cells that color into three fate bands by threshold.

bioelectricMorphologyEditor.title: Rewriting a body's target shape
bioelectricMorphologyEditor.subtitle: Voltage, not DNA, decides how many heads
bioelectricMorphologyEditor.prompt: Set the bioelectric state of the trunk fragment, then regenerate — and try re-cutting the result.
bioelectricMorphologyEditor.aria: A flatworm trunk fragment that regenerates into one head or two depending on its bioelectric state.
bioelectricMorphologyEditor.oneHeadNote: The default target morphology: one head, one tail.
bioelectricMorphologyEditor.twoHeadNote: Flattening the gradient rewrites the target to two heads — no gene was edited.
bioelectricMorphologyEditor.memoryNote: Re-cut in plain water with no further treatment, it regenerates two heads again: the rewritten target is remembered.

swarmSteeringField.title: Steering a swarm you don't command
swarmSteeringField.subtitle: A bias in a few drags the whole school
swarmSteeringField.aria: A school of boids where a fraction feel an attractor and pull the rest into a coordinated turn.
swarmSteeringField.noneNote: No bias: the school mills with no shared direction — separation, alignment, and cohesion alone.
swarmSteeringField.fewNote: Only a few boids feel the attractor, yet alignment and cohesion propagate the pull and the whole school wheels to follow.
swarmSteeringField.manyNote: Most of the school is biased now; the turn is immediate. But even a small fraction was enough — you steer the collective, you never command each animal.
